name: WorkMate.Demo.OrganisationDesigner
displayName: WorkMate demo: organisation designer sample data
description: TEST DATA — not a reference tenant and not part of base.recipe.json. Seeds a small, self-contained Division -> Department -> Section structure with a few placed units and one deliberately unplaced one, so the organisation designer's read-only tree has something real to show. Safe to run on any tenant that has not already used the demo-division/demo-department/demo-section/demo-org codes; it adds data, it does not touch anything else.
author: Aramis Enterprise Solutions
$notes: Not applied automatically by any tenant provisioning flow. An operator runs it deliberately, from the Recipes admin screen or the recipe execution API, against a tenant already running WorkMate.Dimensions.

Exercises the three recipe steps prompt 3 adds: dimension-types, structures, dimension-records. Steps run in that order because structures reference types by code and records reference both types and structures by code, resolved at import — see WorkMate.Dimensions/Recipes.
Every type, structure and record is validated as one batch before anything is written; a single bad row would leave nothing from that step behind, not even the rows before it.
demo-dept-unassigned carries no placement on purpose: it is what a record created outside the designer looks like, and it is what the designer's unplaced-records panel is for.

Three records carry an alias and the rest do not, which is the shape FRS v2.5's own figures show: an alias is optional, and a dimension's list has to read well with the column half empty. demo-div-sales states both halves and demo-dept-retail states only the English one, so the display fallback is exercised by real seeded data rather than only by a unit test.

demo-section allows self-nesting, and demo-sec-counter sits inside demo-sec-instore. That is the FRS's own Department -> HR -> Recruitment shape, and it is what gives one dimension's own tree view a branch to collapse — without it every value is a root of its own tree, which is Rule 2 working correctly and demonstrating nothing. The diagonal is derived from allowsSelfNesting because this structure is still described as a chain; ADR-0010's addendum makes it a cell of the containment grid for a structure described explicitly.

The type codes stay prefixed demo-, as every demo recipe's do: this one is a self-contained SAMPLE rather than a reference company, its selling point is that it runs on any tenant without colliding with anything, and sharing a type code would give that up. Sharing them WAS tried while building slice F2 and reverted — see the Zenith recipe's notes for what it did to the charts. The display names are plain Division, Department and Section again; they briefly said Demo Division, which was an attempt to disambiguate the menu by renaming the data, and decision D23 disambiguates it in the menu instead: types sharing an English singular name are one entry, and its values name the chart they are on.

Section rather than Department, deliberately: adding a unit under a parent that permits two kinds of unit makes the designer's Add-unit form ask which kind, and the browser tests add departments under divisions and sections under departments. Section is the one level nothing in the suite adds beneath, so giving it the diagonal changes no existing journey.
